description:
Repro: def f(x), do: x + 1; main builds {f(1), ..., f(1000)} and prints tuple_size (scratch s75e/gen.py, t1000.fz; budget raised with the spike binary's FZ_SPIKE_BUDGET). fz2 run: EXC_BAD_ACCESS at the stack guard inside fz_closure_get_capture_i64 (lldb, s75e/d7w_lldb.log). fz2 build: the binary exits 139. interp is fine.
Mechanism read from the CLIF dump at N=200 (s75e/t200.clif): main is split into one resume function per element (main__e0__resume_K). Each resume function stores the values computed so far into a stack slot of its own frame (explicit_slot, 869 bytes at K=92, about 9 bytes per held value), tags the slot's address as a closure reference (stack_addr, bor_imm 0x0800...), and calls the next step with call_indirect followed by return. Because the continuation's captures live in the caller's frame the call cannot be a tail call, so N elements nest N native frames, and frame K holds K values: stack use grows with N squared (about 4.5 MB of slots at N=1000, before saved registers). 445 functions at N=200, 424 end in a plain return, 23 tail calls.
Not yet established: which lowering decides stack-allocated continuation captures, and whether the same nesting applies to any long sequence of non-tail calls in one body (inferred yes: the tuple is incidental). Related cost: the same capture-per-step shape is the N^2/2 transport_shape products behind fz-75e.
Blocks the run/build legs of the GH #296 fixture. Fix needs a proposal page.
title: fz2 run and a built binary overflow the stack on a tuple of 1,000 computed elements
